coding.note: Claims are restricted to contributions in the abstract/introduction; the novel blocksparse module is described only in Section 2 and is therefore outside C1's specified scope. No controlled ablations of the abstract's architecture claims are reported. Comparator names cover the main language-model results on pages 6 and 9. Rerun and copied-score coding incorporates the vision results: most baselines were evaluated by the authors, but MM1 scores were copied. Microsoft's independent internal red team is not treated as third-party evaluation. Training seed counts and training compute are not reported; inference hardware/speed does not constitute training compute disclosure. Data categories are disclosed, but not a reconstructible mixture. No explicit renaming of a known technique was identified.

scores_copied.quote:
We just
copied and pasted their published numbers since the model is not publicly available.

claims.quote: We introduce phi-3-mini, a 3.8 billion parameter language model trained on 3.3 trillion tokens,
claims.claim: Introduce phi-3-mini, a small language model with performance rivaling substantially larger models and suitable for local phone deployment.

claims.quote:
Our training dataset
  is a scaled-up version of the one used for phi-2, composed of heavily filtered publicly available web
  data and synthetic data.
claims.claim: Scale up the phi-2 training-data recipe using heavily filtered public web data and synthetic data.

claims.quote: The model is also further aligned for robustness, safety, and chat format.
claims.claim: Further align the model for robustness, safety, and chat use.

claims.quote: We also provide parameter-scaling results with a 7B, 14B models trained for 4.8T tokens,
claims.claim: Provide parameter-scaling results for the more capable 7B phi-3-small and 14B phi-3-medium models.

claims.quote:
To enhance multilingual, multimodal, and long-context
  capabilities, we introduce three models in the phi-3.5 series:
claims.claim: Introduce the phi-3.5 series to enhance multilingual, multimodal, and long-context capabilities.

claims.quote: The phi-3.5-MoE, a 16 x 3.8B MoE model with 6.6 billion active parameters, achieves
claims.claim: Introduce phi-3.5-MoE with 16 experts and 6.6B active parameters, claiming superior reasoning, math, and code performance relative to similarly scaled open models.

claims.quote:
Meanwhile, phi-3.5-Vision, a 4.2 billion parameter model derived from phi-3.5-
  mini, excels in reasoning tasks
claims.claim: Introduce phi-3.5-Vision, derived from phi-3.5-mini, supporting reasoning over single-image and multi-image text prompts.

data_disclosure.quote:
phase-1 comprises mostly of web sources aimed at teaching the model general knowledge and language
understanding.

tokens_disclosed.quote: We trained using bfloat16 for a total of 3.3T tokens.

rerun.quote:
Our performance quality assessment setup used the same evaluation
pipeline for all the baselines to ensure a fair comparison, with the exception of MM1-3B-Chat.
